An expression-level one-line edit above the gold cannot load a class by name (Class.forName and newInstance throw checked exceptions) and cannot reach the private DateTimeZone.getDefaultProvider from another class. The convention is pinned outside the gold: DateTimeZone.getDefaultProvider, which class initialisation still uses, gets the default zone provider by first trying the class named by the system property org.joda.time.DateTimeZone.Provider ('Tries the system property org.joda.time.DateTimeZone.Provider. Then tries a ZoneInfoProvider using the data in org/joda/time/tz/data. Then uses UTCProvider.'); DateTimeZone.getDefaultNameProvider applies the same property-first rule to the name provider, and TestDateTimeZone::testNameProvider asserts it (the named class is used, an unknown class is reported as java.lang.ClassNotFoundException and replaced) and passes; the facade documents null as 'for default'. The gold's javadoc promises the default zone provider, which with the property set to org.joda.time.tz.UTCProvider is a UTCProvider.
